title: Custom Engineered Tissue Culture Molds from Laser-etched Masters
protocol: Assemble the desired mold geometry in vector format using a vector graphics program.
Select File| New and create a canvas of appropriate dimensions with RGB color format.
Create the desired geometry using the shape tools in the left-hand panel.
Enter the desired dimensions at the top of the window to precisely define shape sizes.
Open the color picker and define new color swatches compatible with the laser cutter software.
Prepare the laser cutter according to the manufacturer's specifications.
Ensure sufficient ventilation is used.
Calibrate the bed height to the chosen material thickness.
Open the design file in a vector graphics program on the computer connected to the laser cutter.
Click File| Print and ensure that the laser cutter is set as the printer.
Select "Do Not Scale" in the Scaling drop down menu.
Click the Print button at the bottom of the printing dialog.
In the laser cutter printing utility, click the Settings button.
Assign power settings for each color.
Assign speed settings for each color.
Assign pulses per inch (PPI) settings for each color.
Set cut parameters for design features using appropriate settings.
Set etch parameters for design features using appropriate settings.
Click the large green button to begin laser cutting and etching.
Remove any residual cutting debris from the negative master molds with small brushes and/or compressed air.
Prepare a PDMS casting mix according to its manufacturer's specifications.
Calculate and prepare 0.35 mL/cm2 of PDMS for each master mold.
Degas the prepared PDMS in a vacuum chamber connected to a standard lab vacuum line for 1 hour, or until all bubbles are eliminated.
Tape the outer edge of the mold with vinyl or masking tape such that it extends more than 3 mm above the etched face of the negative master mold.
Press the tape firmly against the side of the mold to prevent leaks later on.
If necessary, apply tape to the bottom of the mold where through-holes are present.
Pour the degassed PDMS over the etched face of the negative master mold.
Place the PDMS-coated negative master mold into a vacuum chamber and degas again for 1 hour, or until all bubbles have been eliminated.
Place the degassed PDMS-coated negative master mold into a 60 °C oven.
Ensure the oven shelf is level.
Alternatively, allow the PDMS to cure at 37 °C overnight.
Or alternatively, allow curing at ambient temperature for ~ 72 h.
Cut multiple molds apart using a razorblade while still on the negative master mold.
Peel each PDMS mold off of the negative master mold carefully.
Trim regions with meniscus from casting that prevent the mold from lying flat.
Remove any excess material or debris using a razor blade.
Prepare molds for cell/tissue casting by autoclaving if necessary.
Adhere molds to the bottom of the desired vessel.
Firmly press new molds against the untreated plastic to adhere them.
Prepare fibrinogen, thrombin, and neutralized collagen casting solutions such that the desired concentration of each will be achieved in the cast tissue.
Keep collagen on ice until casting.
Mix fibrinogen and thrombin immediately prior to casting.
Harvest cells following standard protocols.
Resuspend cells at a concentration appropriate to achieve the desired initial cell density in the cast tissue.
Harvest human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes and keep on ice.
Combine fibrinogen, neutralized collagen, and cell suspension to create a casting mix.
Treat the surfaces of the mold that will be exposed to the casting mix with oxygen plasma for 3-5 seconds.
Alternatively treat the mold surfaces with Pluronic F-127 (1% w/v) surfactant.
Add thrombin to the casting mix immediately prior to casting.
Mix the casting mix thoroughly by pipetting up and down without introducing bubbles.
Pipette the casting mix into the molds, depositing it carefully into all corners and crevices of the mold.
Place the tissue culture vessel in a 37 °C incubator for 45 min.
If the incubator is not well humidified, deposit cell media around the molds prior to incubation.
Return the constructs to the hood after 45 min and cover with cell media before returning to the incubator.
Change the cell media every 48 - 72 h as needed for the cell and construct type.
Wash the molds sequentially with 10% bleach, 70% ethanol, and distilled water after use.
Air dry the molds and autoclave them for re-use up to approximately 10 times.
Collect optical microscopy images of the constructs at time increments ranging from 2 h to 96 h after casting.
Trace the visible construct area in an image analysis suite such as ImageJ.
Analyze the rate and final degree of compaction.
Calibrate both the force transducer and length controller prior to testing.
Turn on the length controller.
Activate the force transducer.
Start the pulse generator.
Initiate the temperature controller.
Fill the mechanical testing trough with Tyrode's solution for engineered cardiac tissues.
Adjust the thermocouple to achieve a bath temperature of 37 °C.
Load a mechanical testing protocol for collecting active contraction data.
Detach the engineered tissue construct from the PDMS mold under a dissection scope.
Transfer the floating freely detached construct to the mechanical testing bath using forceps.
Mount one end of the construct to the hook attached to the force transducer.
Mount the other end of the construct to the hook on the lever arm.
Adjust the lever arm position using the micromanipulator until the construct is positioned without applied strain.
Zero the length controller.
Zero the force controller.
Image the construct through the dissection scope to measure dimensions via image analysis.
Initiate the active force protocol and save collected data upon completion.
Adjust the lever arm until there is zero applied strain if passive mechanical data are required.
Zero the length and force controllers before imaging the construct a second time.
Load and initiate the passive mechanics protocol after adjusting and zeroing.
Transfer the engineered tissue construct to a microcentrifuge tube for fixation using forceps slid between the construct and PDMS mold.
Submerge engineered tissues in 4% paraformaldehyde for 10 min at room temperature.
Rinse the tissues with phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Place a drop of eosin on the tissue and stain it pink for 10 - 30 s.
Rinse the stained tissue with 70% ethanol.
Wrap the tissue in lens paper and place it in a histology cassette using foam pads if necessary to keep the tissue flat.
Submerge the cassette in 70% EtOH and store at 4 °C until ready for paraffin processing.
Bathe samples in 70%, 95%, and 100% ethanol (2 x 30 min each).
Bath samples in three sequential xylene baths for 30 min each.
Submerge the samples in three sequential paraffin baths for 30 min each.
Carefully unfold and remove eosin-stained tissue from lens paper, ensuring it is flat on the bottom of the mold for easier sectioning.
Embed the paraffin-infiltrated tissue in a paraffin block.
Section the tissues using a microtome for desired thickness (5 - 8 µm thick) and stain using standard procedures optimized for the engineered tissue.
Place fixed constructs in 30% sucrose in PBS for 3 h or until equilibrated.
Exchange solution with 50/50 v/v 30% sucrose and OCT freezing medium for 1 h.
Prepare frozen blocks by placing constructs into OCT freezing medium using a 70% EtOH with dry ice slurry for rapid block freezing in plastic trays.
Section the blocks with a cryostat to 10 - 50 µm thick sections.
Orient the tissue sections in the horizontal plane parallel to the mold bottom.
Stain for a marker specific to the cell of interest.
Label f-actin with phalloidin to mark actin stress fibers.
Alternatively, use a cell-specific marker.
Determine orientation by staining sarcomeres with α-actinin if using engineered cardiac tissues.
Assess the major axis of all cells or nuclei in the region of interest manually.
Categorize different regions of the same construct based on geometry.
